ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graphs of the functions $y=3x+b$ and $y=ax-3$ intersect at point $P(-2, -5)$. Based on the graph, what is the solution set of the inequality $3x+b>ax-3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the graphs of the functions $y=3x+b$ and $y=ax-3$ intersect at point $P(-2,-5)$,\\
it follows that the solution set of the inequality $3x+b>ax-3$ is $x>-2$,\\
therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x>-2}$.
